t: Title I of the District of Columbia Revenue Act of 1939 (D.C. Code, sec. 47–134) is repealed.

fable.w: The section simply repeals Title I of the District of Columbia Revenue Act of 1939. It creates no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. The mention of the District of Columbia is only part of the repealed act's name, not an outside-party process.

qwen_block.w: This section simply repeals a previous statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is a legislative action that removes existing law, not a procedural requirement for participation.
qwen_block.s: Title I of the District of Columbia Revenue Act of 1939 (D.C. Code, sec. 47–134) is repealed.

opus.w: The section only repeals Title I of the District of Columbia Revenue Act of 1939. It does not provide for consultation, a hearing, a comment period, rulemaking, an advisory body or a right to sue that would involve anyone outside the federal government. The mention of a revenue law does not create any process for outside parties to take part in a decision.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading:** Because the section mentions a revenue act, someone might think it involves taxpayers or local government in a federal decision. That fails because the section only repeals a title of a statute. It sets up no comment period, hearing, consultation, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue, so no one outside the federal government takes part in any decision.

The repeal is a direct legislative act without any mandated participatory mechanism like a hearing, comment period, or advisory committee.
